item.title: Ralliston's Journey through all of the 001 proposals - Part Three - Dr Gears' Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Review: So I'll start off by saying that I'm very torn on this one.

On one hand, I really like what you're going for here. Yes, it's simple and rather straightforward, but I feel like it fits exactly into the Series I Foundation-verse feel. I like all of the things you present here, and whilst the format screw isn't really as creative those 12 years later, and it's understandable, I feel like the whole article depends just a bit too much on it and in the process sacrifices the mysterious feel all other Series I articles had1. I recognize and respect all of the background stuff, setting the ground for all future in-universe formats and classifications, and I really like them, but even those 12 years ago, it would still feel like not enough. I really, really want to upvote this - but there simply isn't enough. If it had just a bit more background stuff, I'd be happy to upvote it.

Result: A very sad no-vote

Footnotes
1. Which was, in my eyes, their only redeeming quality.

item.title: History is interesting.
item.content:encoded:
The strength of this proposal lies in its unconventionality. This creature isn't a creator, a world destroyer, a nuclear threat to all mankind, etc.. It's simply the first documented discovery of an unexplained anomalous being before the SCP Foundation was christened as such. The articles lack of redactions, standard format, and historical footnotes throughout ("Dr. Hermann Keter", "…conversion of ADRX-19 to a dedicated recovery and containment facility") are a treat to read.

I find it to be a clever proposal. I'd certainly prefer reading about the first SCP in this format, rather than a tale discussing the history of the foundation. It's like stumbling upon old photographs or diary entries— you get to experience the report exactly as it was written decades ago.

item.title: Re: A Late Dissenter
item.content:encoded:
To offer a counter argument…

If you were hiding the real SCP-001 among a bunch of decoys, it'd be better if you put some things in the archive that had some veracity to them, so anybody doing the research and looking for the "truth" would get caught up on them. djkaktus I does something like this, with O5-2 making the follow order:

I've allowed clearance in the database for the creation of a number of false objects in the slot; if anybody gets that far, that should be enough to satiate them. I pulled out some of the original -EX's to hold the spot until we can find something better.

With that in mind, throwing the first anomaly ever contained into the list of 001s makes sense: if somebody comes in and finds it among the rest, they won't be surprised. It entirely works for belonging in the archives, and is therefore a good entry to act as a pseudo-fake.

tl;dr - it's not among the fakes because it needs to be concealed, it's the concealment itself (and that doesn't mean it has to be false)

item.title: A Late Dissenter
item.content:encoded:
From what I understand, regardless of which entry is the "real" entry, SCP 001 is canonically hidden among numerous fake entries. Therefore, I think it is fair to say that all SCP 001 entries need to A) Make sense as to why the Foundation would hide it's existence if were the true entry, and B) Be reasonable enough to trick to someone into believing it to be the true SCP 001 even if it was a fake. In my opinion, this entry fails in both those respects:

A) Why would the Foundation hide this? It doesn't paint them in a negative light, doesn't have information leading to a super weapon, nor would knowledge of it lead to mass hysteria among Foundation staff. The Prototype is no more dangerous than the average Euclid in any way I can think of, and I simply see no reason why the Foundation would go to such great lengths to hide this SCP's existence.

B) Who would fall for this? The only reason I can think of is that The Prototype is real, having been added in as a red herring. So that when when a curios researcher stumble across this entry, and finds it's contents to be demonstrably true, they'd be happy and go home. Except they wouldn't, because the only way for this to be the sole true SCP 001 is that the Foundation felt like trolling the researchers. Anyone smart enough to be a researcher probably isn't going to fall for such a simple trick, and is just going to continue looking into the validity of the other SCP 001 entries anyways.

While this article is very well written, it neither makes sense as the true entry nor as a fake. I'll admit that this may come down to a lack of imagination on my part, but I haven't seen anything that voids my complaints concerning this article since I originally read the it. If any of the claims I made above are false, then I would appreciate someone explaining where I've gone wrong.

item.title: Re: not_a_seagull'a SCP Oddessy: Dr. Gears' Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Honestly this article captures my imagination. People complain there's no story to this? No….what this article does is cause you to CREATE a story surrounding it.

This was the first article they wrote…was this the first anomalous item they had ever encountered? Somehow I doubt it, because it sounds like they existed as an organization already. They probably formed BECAUSE they had been getting so many reports of anomalous phenomena.

Was this the first one they ever captured/contained? Maybe. Maybe not. Maybe it's simply the first one they felt they needed to write a document about detailing what the object was, what it does, and how to keep it in containment. As noted, the name of the article is "The Prototype". Obviously the object itself isn't a prototype. Thus this is in reference to the documentation. The Foundation might have captured dozens of items leading up to this point, but only just now were they making an effort toward creating detailed documentation of the objects.

In the end it's a fantastic article. Gears is one of the best authors on the wiki, he's capable of writing something VASTLY scarier/more interesting with a better story. But THAT ISN'T THE POINT. He wrote exactly what was needed for this, and nothing more. I remember reading this back when I first joined and just passing over it because I didn't really get what made it special. Now with years and years and thousands of articles of context….yeah, this one is awesome.

item.title: not_a_seagull'a SCP Oddessy: Dr. Gears' Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Item #: SCP-001 (Dr Gears' Proposal)

Author: Dr Gears

Review:

+ Review
- Review

Now, I upvoted this. Not because of any special gimmicks or cool story, but because, in my mind, it just makes sense. Logically, in an organization as organized as the Foundation, SCP-001 wouldn't be the most important anomaly, or the anomaly that created all anomalies. It would be the first anomaly.

The SCP itself is very bland. It's a demon that creates wormholes that shoot radiation. The thing is, it's the first time they encountered anything anomalous. They reacted to it and captured it like it was the first time they found something out of the norm. This thing, in universe, predates the SCP designation itself.

The last line is what does it for me. They're realizing that other anomalous phenomena, SCP-002 and SCP-003 and so on, all exist. And they gotta get ready for 'Em. This is like forshadowing for the entire Foundation. And that's why I upvoted.

Verdict: Upvote

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm sad to say that I downvoted this article.
Now, I'll focus on the positives first; the things that I did enjoy about the article. The concept itself is one that I find amusing; the notion that SCP-001 isn't some sort of uber-dangerous entity that prompted the creation of the Foundation, or an explanation for the existence of the anomalous, but simply the first skip cataloged. It's a simple yet entertaining idea, due mainly to the fact that it's so underwhelming. It's not a giant death-angel wielding a fire-saber, nor is it a sentient, malevolent factory capable of churning out skips… it's what the 001 slot would logically be.
But that's my main problem with the article.
It's underwhelming.
The other 001 proposals… they all evoke some sort of emotional reaction from me. Whether it be awe from Clef's Gate Guardian, or shock at sandrewswann's fourth-wall breakage, they all made me feel something. This one… it just doesn't do much for me. I get what you were trying to do, but the purposely messy, scatterbrained document is still messy and scatterbrained, even if it was intentional. With all the other proposals, I can just sense that the writers poured hours and hours of toil and revisions into it, that it's a labor of love, and the pinnacle of one's writing career on the site. With this one, though, I don't get that feeling. This feels far inferior to some of your greater works, Gears.
TL;DR: I liked the idea, but the article wasn't interesting to me.
